title: The Ben & Marc Show: China Has Scale. Can America Catch Up?

reader_summary.headline: Russia today is out producing NATO on 155 munitions and took about two years.
reader_summary.overview: Russia today is out producing NATO on 155 munitions and took about two years. We have no strategic plan as a country for how we preserve supply in a catastrophic situation. Every world game we run out of munitions missiles in like six to seven days.

key_points.text: Every world game we run out of munitions missiles in like six to seven days.
key_points.evidence_quote: Every world game we run out of munitions missiles in like six to seven days, and then it takes about two to three years to refill that battery.

key_points.text: We shoot all our missiles in one week and then we have none for two years.
key_points.evidence_quote: We shoot all our missiles in one week and then we have none for two years.

key_points.text: If the next conflict demands both brains and bulk, can the US combine innovation with industrial scale faster enough to win?
key_points.evidence_quote: If the next conflict demands both brains and bulk, can the US combine innovation with industrial scale faster enough to win?

key_points.text: On this episode of The Ben and Mark Show, we're joined by Brian Shim, co-founder and CEO of Andrewville, and Chris Power.
key_points.evidence_quote: On this episode of The Ben and Mark Show, we're joined by Brian Shim, co-founder and CEO of Andrewville, and Chris Power, founder and CEO of Hadrian.

thesis: The speakers argue that the US has lost its industrial manufacturing scale and skilled workforce due to decades of outsourcing and a strategic over-reliance on technical superiority rather than mass production, a lesson definitively proven by the war in Ukraine. They contend that rebuilding this capacity will require time to retrain the workforce and re-shore production, starting with national interest sectors like defense and aerospace before expanding to commercial manufacturing.
